title: Turn CSV rows into records
hints: `zip(keys, row)` pairs each column name with the value in the same position.
Clean the header once up front with a list comprehension. Then build each record with a dict comprehension over `zip(keys, row)`.
`keys = [h.strip().lower() for h in header]` then `return [{k: v.strip() for k, v in zip(keys, row)} for row in rows if len(row) == len(keys)]`
